question.text: Will Applied Materials' Q1 FY2027 revenue guidance midpoint be at or above $11.0 billion?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves on the total revenue guidance for Applied Materials' fiscal Q1 2027 (the first quarter of fiscal year 2027) contained in Applied Materials' fourth quarter and fiscal 2026 earnings press release, scheduled for Thursday, November 12, 2026 and published at https://ir.appliedmaterials.com/news-releases (expected title: "Applied Materials Announces Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2026 Results"). The guidance midpoint is the center of the guided revenue range: the stated center figure when guidance is given in the form "Total revenue $X +/- $Y" (e.g., "$10,750 +/- $500 million" has a midpoint of $10,750 million), the arithmetic mean of the low and high ends when guidance is given as a range, and the stated figure itself when guidance is given as a single value. The question resolves YES if that midpoint is at or above $11,000 million (e.g., a midpoint of $11,000 million or $11,250 million resolves YES; $10,750 million resolves NO). If the press release contains no fiscal Q1 2027 revenue guidance, revenue guidance for that quarter given in Applied Materials' Q4 FY2026 earnings call or its prepared remarks (both posted at https://ir.appliedmaterials.com) will be used; if no such guidance is published, the question is annulled. If the Applied Materials page is unavailable, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting the guidance will be used.
question.fine_print: Guidance refers to Applied Materials' own total (company-wide) revenue outlook for fiscal Q1 2027 — not segment-level guidance, not the fiscal Q4 2026 results themselves, and not third-party consensus estimates.

research:
I could not find any fiscal Q1 2027 guidance yet. It first appears in the November 12, 2026 release, so nothing settles the question now. Management has only said Q1 will grow sequentially. To reach $11.0B, the midpoint must be about 7.3% above the Q4 guide midpoint of $10.25B, in a 14-week quarter.

The segment guides are Semiconductor Systems about $7.9B, Applied Global Services (AGS) about $1.84B and Other about $510M. The source is the earnings call transcript. [Investing.com transcript](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-applied-materials-beats-q3-2026-estimates-shares-fall-93CH-4859444)

### 2. Current status

He said the 14-week quarter brings "a higher than average step-up in our Q1 operating expenses." He added that the extra week helps services, but "not so much on the equipment side." That suggests the extra week may lift revenue by less than the full 1/13. [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-applied-materials-beats-q3-2026-estimates-shares-fall-93CH-4859444)

[Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-applied-materials-beats-q3-2026-estimates-shares-fall-93CH-4859444)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)

It reported the 50-day moving average at $457.66. [Markets Daily](https://www.themarketsdaily.com/2026/11/01/applied-materials-nasdaqamat-stock-falls-7-5-whats-next.html)
- 2026-10-29: KLA guided its December quarter to $4.7B +/- $200M. That is about 13.5% above its September-quarter revenue of $4.14B and about 42.5% higher year over year. [Fool transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/29/kla-klac-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/), [FourWeekMBA](https://fourweekmba.com/ai-kla-guides-to-a-4-7b-quarter-implying-43-annual-growth/)

At the Oct 13 SEMICON West investor presentation, management targeted about 54% gross margin and 40% operating margin by 2030 and expected wafer fab equipment (WFE) to grow faster than in the last decade. It gave no specific WFE forecast. Consensus for Q4 is about $10.30B revenue and $4.06 EPS. [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/applied-materials-sinks-17-week-090603850.html)

### 4. Base rates
- The guidance midpoints in the FY2026 sequence rose each quarter. The Q3 and Q4 figures are verified; Q1 and Q2 are from memory and the percentages derived from them are approximate:
  - Q1 FY26 (Nov 2025): about $6.85B
  - Q2 (Feb 2026): about $7.65B, up about 12%
  - Q3 (May 2026): $8.95B, up about 17%
  - Q4 (Aug 2026): $10.25B, up 14.5%
- Applied guides in $250M steps with a +/- $500M band, so $11.0B is the first step above $10.75B.
- Reaching $11.0B needs a midpoint about 7.3% above the Q4 guide. If Q4 actual revenue beats the guide by a typical amount (about $165M, as in Q3), the needed step falls to roughly 5.8-6%. Applied has beaten EPS consensus in each of the last 4 quarters, by about 3-8%. [MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/AMAT/earnings/)
- Earlier January-quarter guides were much smaller. For example, FY2025 Q1 was guided at $6.75-7.55B. [search result](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4408079-applied-materials-drives-q1-2025-revenue-up-7-but-q2-outlook-falls-below-estimates)
- Peer December-quarter guides were mixed: KLA about +13.5% sequential, Lam about +5%.
- The last 53-week fiscal year was FY2021, whose Q1 had 14 weeks; its guide in Nov 2020 beat estimates. [BNN Bloomberg](https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/applied-materials-gives-sales-forecast-that-tops-estimates-1.1521782)
- Consensus for the January 2027 quarter is $10.74B (Zacks, 9 estimates, high $11.20B), from the question background. Consensus for fiscal 2027 is about $46.4B, up about 35%.

### 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi's "What will Applied Materials say" market for the Nov 12 call is a mention market only, not a revenue market. Yes prices include EPIC Center 0.90, Agentic 0.79 and Hybrid Bonding 0.77. It does not bear directly on this question.
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on AMAT's Q1 FY27 revenue guidance.
- I found no named sell-side Q1 FY27 guide estimate beyond the consensus figures above.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-12, after the close: Applied's Q4 FY2026 release and the 4:30 p.m. ET call, which resolve the question.
- Before then: possible US export-control legislation or rules on China (about 26-28% of revenue). Any such action could make management more cautious in its guide.
- Other news on hyperscaler AI capex and memory capex could set the tone.

- Recent sequential steps in the guide midpoint were about 12-14.5%. That compares with Lam's reported December guide of about +5% and KLA's of about +13.5%.
- The 14-week quarter mechanically adds about 7.7% more days. Management has said the extra week mostly lifts services revenue (about $1.84B per quarter), so it would add only about $0.14B.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain. The outcome will be known after the market close on November 12, 2026, when Applied releases its Q4 FY2026 results. For Yes, the fiscal Q1 2027 total revenue guidance midpoint must be at least $11,000M. That is about 7.3% above the Q4 guide midpoint of $10.25B, or about 5 to 6% above a likely Q4 actual of roughly $10.4 to 10.5B.

(b) Status quo: no guidance exists yet. If management simply meets consensus of $10.74B, or guides a modest sequential rise like Lam's, the midpoint lands near $10.75 to 10.95B, which resolves No. A straight continuation of the recent guide momentum (each quarterly guide up about $1.3B) would give Yes.

(c) Base rate: there are two reference classes.
- In the current upcycle, Applied's sequential guide-to-guide steps have been about 12%, 17% and 14.5%. All exceeded 7.3%, so this class says 3 of 3 for Yes.
- Over a longer history, January-quarter guides are usually flat to modest sequential steps. A 7%+ step happens maybe 30 to 35% of the time.

Blending the two, I start near 50%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- 2026-08-13: management expects Q1 sequential growth and calls 2027 "another strong record year."
- Q1 is a 14-week quarter, which adds roughly $140M or more to services revenue.
- 2026-10-29: KLA guided its December quarter up about 13.5% sequentially.
- The consensus high is $11.20B, and fiscal 2027 consensus of about $46B implies run-rates above $11B.

Evidence for No:
- 2026-10-21: Lam, the closest peer in deposition and etch, guided only about +5% sequentially.
- The CFO said the extra week does not help equipment much.
- Clean-room constraints may cap shipments.
- Consensus for the January quarter is $10.74B, below the threshold.
- The stock fell about 24% from October 12 to October 24, which suggests expectations are being reset lower.
- China export-control risk could make management cautious.

(e) No scenario: Q4 comes in at $10.45B and management guides $10.85B +/- $500M, citing clean-room timing and lumpy semiconductor systems revenue.
Yes scenario: Q4 comes in at $10.5B, semiconductor systems keeps ramping on DRAM and advanced packaging, the extra week lifts services, and the guide is $11.15B +/- $500M.

(f) There is no matching prediction market to anchor to. The arithmetic puts $11.0B almost exactly at the center:
- A Lam-like +5% step on a roughly $10.45B Q4 actual gives about $10.97B.
- Adding the extra week of services takes that to about $11.1B.
- Consensus of $10.74B sits slightly below the threshold, but Applied has tended to guide above consensus in this cycle.

The considerations roughly balance, so I stay near 50%, shading slightly below because the peer guide and consensus both sit under the threshold.

Probability: 48%

(a) About 10 days remain. The outcome is known after the close on Nov 12, 2026, when Applied's Q4 FY26 release comes out. For Yes, the fiscal Q1 2027 total revenue guide midpoint must be at least $11,000M. That is at least 7.3% above the Q4 guide midpoint of $10,250M, and roughly 5-6% above likely Q4 actual revenue if Q4 beats as usual.

(b) There is no Q1 guide yet. Simply extending the trend does not give a status quo answer. Consensus ($10.74B) sits slightly below the threshold, while weekly run-rate math for a 14-week quarter ($11.04B) sits slightly above it.

(c) Base rate: Applied's FY2026 guide midpoints rose 12-17% sequentially each quarter (about $6.85B, $7.65B, $8.95B, $10.25B). A step of about 7% is well below that pace, which favors Yes. Against that, guides that clear the published consensus by about 2.5% happen perhaps 40-50% of the time in up-cycles. Blending these gives a base rate of about 50%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - Aug 13: management said to expect sequential growth in Q1, a 14-week quarter, and "another strong record year in 2027."
  - Oct 29: KLA guided its December quarter about 13.5% sequential, showing peer strength.
  - FY27 consensus of about $45.6-46.4B implies an average of about $11.4-11.6B per quarter, which is consistent with Q1 at or above $11.0B.
  - The guide trajectory has been 12-17% per quarter.
- **For No:**
  - Aug 13: CFO Hill said the extra week helps services "not so much on the equipment side."
  - Clean-room constraints may limit shipments.
  - Oct 21: Lam guided only about +5% sequential.
  - Zacks January-quarter consensus is $10.74B.
  - Possible conservatism given China export-control risk and a weak stock.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** Q4 comes in at $10.45B. Management guides Q1 to $10.80B +/- $500M, citing an equipment ramp weighted to the second half of 2027 and minimal benefit from the extra week. The midpoint is $10.80B.
- **Yes:** Q4 beats at $10.5B. AI logic, DRAM/HBM and advanced packaging momentum, plus services gaining from the extra week, lead to a guide of $11.15B +/- $500M.

(f) Starting from about 50%, I move up modestly. Applied's sequential guide growth has been far above the roughly 7% required, KLA's strong December guide shows the cycle is still accelerating, and FY27 consensus implies Q1 near $11B. I temper this because of Hill's explicit caution on the equipment extra week, Lam's tepid guide, and a consensus below threshold that the company might simply meet. There is no liquid market on this question to anchor to.

Probability: 55%

**(a) Timing and what Yes requires.** The outcome is known about 10 days from now, on Nov 12, 2026, after the market close. Yes requires the Q4 FY26 release (or the call) to guide fiscal Q1 2027 total revenue with a midpoint of at least $11,000M. Applied guides in $250M steps, so the realistic midpoints are $10.75B, $11.0B, $11.25B and so on, and $11.0B or higher resolves Yes.

**(b) Status quo.** No guide exists yet. Mechanically extending the current trajectory points close to the threshold:
- The Q4 guide is $10.25B over 13 weeks.
- Holding that weekly rate flat across a 14-week quarter gives about $11.04B.
- Consensus is $10.74B.

**(c) Base rate.** Applied's FY26 sequential guide-midpoint increases were about 12%, 17% and 14.5%. Reaching $11.0B needs only about 7.3% over the Q4 guide midpoint, or about 6% over a likely beat on actual Q4 revenue. In up-cycles, Applied's guides have usually come in at or above consensus. The one comparable 14-week Q1, in FY2021, was guided about 9% above the prior quarter's actuals and topped estimates. On this reference class alone, Yes is somewhat favored, around 60%.

**(d) Strongest evidence.**
- For Yes:
  - On Oct 29, 2026, KLA guided its December quarter about 13.5% higher sequentially.
  - On Aug 13, 2026, the CFO said Applied expects sequential growth in Q1 and "another strong record year in 2027."
  - The extra week adds revenue.
  - Consensus for fiscal 2027 of about $46B implies a run-rate above $11B per quarter.
- For No:
  - On Aug 13, 2026, the CFO said the extra week helps services "not so much on the equipment side," and that clean-room limits will cap shipments.
  - On Oct 21, 2026, Lam guided its December quarter up only about 5% sequentially.
  - The January-quarter consensus of $10.74B sits below the threshold.
  - The stock has dropped sharply since Oct 12, which may signal that analysts and investors expect a cautious tone.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- No: Q4 comes in at about $10.4B. Management cites clean-room timing and China export-control uncertainty and guides $10.75B +/- $500M, about 3% sequential growth, roughly matching consensus.
- Yes: Q4 comes in at about $10.5B on strong DRAM and advanced-packaging demand. Management guides $11.25B +/- $500M, helped by the extra week and AGS growth.

**(f) Adjustment.** I start near 60% from the momentum in Applied's guides and KLA's strong peer guide. I move down about 5 points because consensus sits below $11.0B, the CFO played down the extra week's effect on equipment, and Lam's guide was modest. No prediction market covers this question, so there is no market anchor.

Probability: 55%
